scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Gair dance emerged from the Bhil community in Rajasthan, India, and gradually gained widespread adoption across the entire state.
Although practiced by diverse communities across Rajasthan, it has developed especially strong roots in the Mewar and Marwar regions.
The dance reflects enduring communal heritage and martial traditions, with local lore suggesting historic connections to scenes from the war front.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Gair dance is closely associated with major festive occasions, prominently the spring festival of Holi during February and March, as well as Janmashtami.
Locals consider Janmashtami incomplete without the staging of Gair.
Although staged at any time for entertainment, the dance carries symbolic associations with warfare, appearing to evoke battlefield maneuvers.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform in large circular formations, striking slender wooden sticks called khanda against those of other dancers.
When performed jointly by men and women, participants initially form two concentric rings, with the women comprising a smaller inner ring surrounded by the men.
The dancers move in a clockwise direction before reversing into a counter-clockwise path, coordinating their footwork with the striking of sticks and drumbeats.
Watch for Half-swirl, Khanda striking.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The musical accompaniment for Gair dance relies on traditional Rajasthani percussion and wind instruments.
The ensemble features the dhol, nagada, and dholak, which establish the driving percussive rhythm, alongside the flute.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Men generally wear long, pleated tunics designed to flare out into full-length skirts during spins and half-swirls.
Bhil dancers wear brightly coloured traditional attire and may carry accessories including arrows, swords, and wooden sticks.
The sticks, known as khanda, are harvested from the Gundi tree, require minimal cleaning, and are cut thin and light to enhance speed and visual flare.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Regional styles of Gair vary by rhythm, circular formations, and attire across Rajasthan.
Gair originated directly from the folk dances of the indigenous Bhil community of Rajasthan, later branching into regional variants like Dandi Gair and Geendad across various communities.

Gair dance is a traditional folk dance from Rajasthan, India, performed by men wearing long skirts and turbans, carrying sticks, and forming a circle. They stamp their feet, twirl their sticks, and engage in mock fights while accompanied by traditional music. It is performed during festive occasions and celebrates the bravery of the Rajasthani people.
